statement: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.

An input string is valid if open brackets are closed by the same type of bracket, open brackets are closed in the correct order, and every close bracket has a corresponding open bracket of the same type.
problem.summary: Given a string of only '()[]{}', return whether the brackets are valid: every open bracket is closed by the same type, in the correct order.
problem.optimal: Single pass with a stack: push open brackets, and on a close bracket check the top of the stack matches; valid iff the stack is empty at the end. O(n) time, O(n) space.
problem.pitfalls: Popping from an empty stack on a leading close bracket like ')('; forgetting the final stack-empty check for unclosed brackets like '('; only counting bracket totals (fails '([)]'); slow repeated string replacement of '()' pairs instead of a stack.

variant.title: Template Delimiter Audit
brief: Our templating engine lets authors wrap expressions in three kinds of delimiters: round, square and curly. Before a template is saved, a lint step strips everything except the delimiters and checks that the author opened and closed them properly.

Implement delimitersNestCleanly(s), where s is the stripped string made up only of the characters ( ) [ ] { }, and return true if every opening delimiter is closed by one of the same kind with the pairs properly nested, or false otherwise.
variant.contract: delimitersNestCleanly(s) receives a string of only the characters ( ) [ ] { } and returns true exactly when every closing delimiter matches the most recently opened unclosed delimiter of the same kind and nothing is left open at the end; a stray closer, a mismatched or overlapping pair, or an unclosed opener returns false.

clarifications.question: Can pairs overlap, like a round pair that starts inside a square pair but ends outside it?
clarifications.answer: No. Overlapping pairs such as ([)] are invalid; a pair must close entirely inside the pair that contains it.

clarifications.question: What if a closing delimiter shows up with nothing open?
clarifications.answer: The template is invalid, so return false.

clarifications.question: What if something is still open when the string ends?
clarifications.answer: That is also invalid; return false.

clarifications.question: Could there be other characters mixed in?
clarifications.answer: No. The lint step has already removed everything except the six delimiter characters.

clarifications.question: How long can the string be?

followUps: Authors now want the error message to point at the position of the first offending delimiter. What would you change?
Suppose string literals in the template can contain delimiters that should be ignored, escaped with a backslash. How does that affect your check?
If only one kind of delimiter were allowed, could you do this with less memory?
hints: Walk through {[]} by hand. When you reach the first closing delimiter, which opening delimiter does it have to match?
Of all the delimiters still open at any moment, which one is the only one allowed to be closed next?
What do you need to remember about the open delimiters so each closer can be checked, and what must be true of that memory once you reach the end?
